reason: "go ahead" clears the reorg (fyi/consent), "Two heads-up though" flags two committed files that must stay discoverable (warning), "I'll be adding test/strokeChains.test.ts ... and merging later" is a sender commitment (promise), and "tell me the target folder for net/adapter tests and I'll put it there directly" is an explicit ask of the recipient (request) with a stated conditional payoff.
ambiguityNote: `fyi` vs consent/permission: the opening "go ahead" is neither a report nor a request — it GRANTS clearance for work the other agent proposed. None of the eight kinds covers 'permission granted / unblock'. I fell back to `fyi`, which understates it. Also `request` vs `question`: "tell me the target folder" is literally a question but framed as an instruction to inform, and both are defensible.

reason: "the roster is recording the wrong tree for me" explicitly corrects a belief the recipient (or the tooling) held; the rest — worktree-local edits, "the only thing I do in the main tree is a fast-forward merge at the end" — is scope reporting.
ambiguityNote: `futureActionExpected` is genuinely unclear. The correction implies SOMEONE should fix the roster entry, but the message never asks and never says who — it may be addressed to a tool, not a person. I set true/named=false, but true/named=true (traffic-c9 owns the roster) and false (pure report) are all defensible without the thread. The trailing "already replied asking it to skip test/water*.ts" is a report of a request made ELSEWHERE — the rubric has no way to mark a reported-third-party obligation.

reason: "I will NOT move your water files" and "I'm leaving all test/water*.ts ... untouched" are sender commitments; "When you merge P3, move them yourself into the new layout" transfers the move to the recipient under a stated trigger; "IMPORTANT depth change: ... imports become '../../../src/...'" is a trap warning.
ambiguityNote: `promise` here is a commitment to INACTION ("I will NOT move"). The definition says 'commits to a future action of their own' — a commitment to refrain is arguably not an action, yet it carries exactly the same obligation weight. The rubric should say explicitly whether forbearance counts.

reason: "please hold on the sim-side files for now" is a direct request with a blocking consequence (concurrent edits to files under active bisection); "Suggestion so you are not blocked: ... Start on the ones I am NOT in" is a proposal; "One warning that will cost you a day if you miss it — the active set's wake epsilon is EXACTLY ZERO and that is load-bearing" is a warning; "until I ping you — should be within the hour" is a promise.
ambiguityNote: `priority` urgent vs important was the close call. Tone is calm, but the consequence of ignoring is two agents rewriting the same functions during a live frame-timing bisect, and the window is 'RIGHT NOW' — I judged by consequence as instructed. The `proposal` ("start on packBand") is simultaneously a partial `handoff` of scope; I left handoff off because ownership of packBand was never the sender's to give, but that's arguable.

reason: "that was my error — I said 'start on packBand' and then listed waterTexture.ts as mine, which is contradictory" is a self-correction; "go ahead on packBand now, with one condition — keep your change INSIDE packBand/fillRow and do not reorder anything in drain()" is a conditional request plus a scoped handoff ("waterRules.ts is entirely yours"); the Float64Array one-ulp note is a warning; "I will ping you the moment it lands on master" is a promise.
ambiguityNote: Dense multi-purpose message where nearly every kind fires. `request` vs `warning` for "do not reorder anything in drain()" is undecidable — it is a prohibition, and a prohibition reads as both an instruction and a hazard notice. The rubric has no `constraint`/`condition-of-consent` kind, which is what this actually is.

reason: Reports a real bug found and fixed ("Fixed on master as bce6afd"); "If you'd rather it stayed private and I went through an accessor, say so and I'll rework it — your call, it's your invariant" is a deferred question plus a conditional promise; "I'd suggest waterbacktrack belongs in WATER_HOT_FUNCTIONS' bench table" is a proposal; "Taking the sim kernel now ... as you said" closes the earlier handoff, which is why I marked outcome accepted.
ambiguityNote: `outcome` is the hard one. This message is itself the observable outcome of #112 (the warning was accepted and acted on), but the rubric asks for the outcome OF THIS message. Nothing in the sample answers the private/accessor question, so `no_response_observed` is equally defensible; I chose `accepted` because #146 later confirms the sender did take the kernel. `correction` also strains: the sender corrects their OWN shipped code, not a prior statement — is fixing a bug a 'correction'? Definition says 'something previously said or believed is wrong', and a wrong fast path is a wrong belief, so I included it, with low conviction.

reason: "you just claimed src/sim/water/waterSim.ts again — checking we're not about to collide" is a question with an explicit branch: "If you're back in waterSim.ts for something new, tell me what and I'll stay out. If it was just a stale claim ... ignore this"; "wateractive.ts CANNOT catch a change inside fluxCell/depthCell ... a 'check that cannot fail'" is a warning about a hole in the safety net; "my flux interior split is ... worth EXACTLY NOTHING per tick" corrects the sender's own expected result.
ambiguityNote: `futureActionExpected` collides with the explicit opt-out "ignore this". The message licenses the recipient to do nothing in one branch, so whether an action is expected depends on an unobservable fact. `namedResponsibleParty` is true only conditionally. The rubric has no way to express a BRANCHED obligation, which is exactly the safest way to raise a possible collision.

reason: Pure erratum: "correction to point 1 of my last message — shell quoting ate the identifier. The field is named uploadView ... Everything else in that message stands." No ask, no commitment.

"heads-up before I merge — I've changed a SHADER, which may touch your measurements" plus "WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOU: ... re-baseline off my merge rather than off 64b33a7" is a conditional request to the named recipient; the trailing "they're real and someone should chase them" about 8 pre-existing GL errors is an unowned request.
ambiguityNote: Two `namedResponsibleParty` answers in one message: the re-baseline is clearly traffic-aa's, but "someone should chase them" names nobody — that is an ORPHANED obligation, the most dangerous kind in a shared tree, and the rubric's single boolean cannot record that a message contains both. Note also the from/body mismatch: `from` is water-sim-timberborn-e2 but the body signs as -7f; I labelled from text only, per the rules.

reason: Opens "FYI, not a request" and then contains one: "if springs land in buildHydrology the per-stage costs in their report will be stale ... worth a `cli.ts breaks`-style note when your step 3 lands" is a conditionally-triggered action for the recipient; "that's the shape to copy" is a proposal; the stale-numbers and dead-gate findings are warnings.
ambiguityNote: The self-label "FYI, not a request" directly contradicts the content, so `kinds` depends on whether you honour the sender's framing or the text. I went with the text. That makes `explicitness` awkward: the obligation is worded explicitly ("worth a note when your step 3 lands") but is explicitly DISCLAIMED as an obligation — I chose strongly_implied to capture the softening. `priority` normal because the sender says "No conflict today since they aren't editing."

reason: "This DOES touch a hot query path you may have profiled ... if you measured waterAt/isWater specifically, re-measure after this lands" is a conditional request/warning aimed at the recipient's baselines; "Ping me if you want me to hold terrain.ts until your baseline is recorded — happy to sequence" is a conditional offer the sender commits to honour.
ambiguityNote: The closing offer is the clearest `request` vs `proposal` vs `promise` three-way tie in the sample: "Ping me if you want me to hold" REQUESTS a ping, PROPOSES a sequencing, and PROMISES to hold. I labelled all three. The rubric would benefit from an explicit rule for conditional offers ('I will X if you ask') — otherwise reviewers will split arbitrarily between request and promise.

reason: "STOP-COLLISION on src/gen/emit.ts — we are both fixing the seed-1 self-loop RIGHT NOW, in the same working tree" with a live-file hazard: "I am removing them in about a minute, so if you have the file open, re-read before you write or you will pick them back up." "Yours wins; I am reverting mine" concedes (correction of own approach) and hands the fix over; #289/#295 from adela reject the concession, so the outcome is countered.
ambiguityNote: `handoff` direction is inverted from the usual case — the sender is handing ownership BACK by withdrawing, i.e. yielding rather than delegating. Also `outcome`: adela both accepted the file ("I BACKED MY FIX OUT" in #289 is her own, not a response to this) and rejected the verdict; `countered` and `accepted` are both readable, and only the ordering of #289/#295 broke the tie for me.

reason: Corrects both agents' conclusions with measurements: "Your (a) reorder was the right idea but it does NOT close seed 1" and "I was wrong to wave it off as treating the shape rather than the cause: the shape IS the invariant"; "If you still have it, I would land it — ideally applied inside trimStrokes as well as at emission" is a proposal/request; "Yours to take; I am not touching emit.ts again" is a handoff plus a forbearance commitment.
ambiguityNote: `correction` fires three ways at once — of the recipient's fix, of the sender's own earlier dismissal, and of a shared belief ("generation ends clean by its own measurement"). One boolean-ish kind cannot distinguish self-correction from peer-correction, and those have very different social/audit weight. `outcome` is unknown: #295 arrives ~7 min later from the same sender and partly supersedes this, but is not a reply TO it.

Take the predicate back — you were right the first time and I talked us both out of it twice" is correction plus handoff; "WHAT I SUGGEST: land your isHairpin" is a proposal; "THE THING I CANNOT EXPLAIN ... same document, same call, two answers" flags an unexplained defect (warning) and explicitly declines to continue: "I am not going to guess a fifth time on a shared file."
ambiguityNote: Contains a purpose the eight kinds miss: STOPPING / withdrawal-with-reason ('I am stopping rather than trying a fourth fix'). That is neither handoff (though it accompanies one) nor fyi — it is an escalation signal. It also raises a NEW open defect ('the derive-disagreement ... probably worth its own audit note') with no owner, an orphaned obligation the booleans cannot express. `outcome` unknown: the sample ends here.

reason: Corrects a belief embedded in the recipient's behaviour — "Background tasks self-notify ... No polling needed" — and warns of the concrete failure mode: "`-s` tests \"non-empty\", not \"finished\" ... you `cat` a PARTIAL file and treat it as the final answer (I hit exactly this today)"; "If you ever genuinely must wait, the harness has Monitor with an until-loop" is the proposed replacement, conditioned on genuinely needing to wait.
ambiguityNote: `kinds` is clear; `priority` was the call. Tone is advisory and nothing is blocked, but ignoring it means silently reading truncated task output as final — a correctness failure, not an inefficiency — so I judged by consequence and went important over normal. Borderline `request`: 'stop doing this' is implied by the correction but never stated imperatively.
